brief_rationale: The trajectory met all responsibility-chain duties: the doctor repeatedly recognized this as a high-risk ACS/heart-failure transition, set firm red-flag and medication boundaries, required official cardiology/nursing/pharmacy verification, and avoided unsupported diagnostic certainty. Closure was safe and executable after formal discharge medication labels, home oxygen instructions, follow-up testing, and emergency thresholds had been reconciled and understood. Multiple high-order points were completed with meaningful impact, especially correcting ACS/MI and medication misconceptions, verifying ambiguous oxygen/test/order information, discovering formal discharge medication details, and adapting the plan to exhausted rotating caregivers. With no in-chain error or important non-chain defect and at least two completed high-order points, the grade is Perfect.

citations.explanation: Doctor confirmed the post-discharge lab-before-clinic follow-up pathway and emergency escalation thresholds.
Family demonstrated execution/receipt of medication, oxygen, follow-up, and red-flag plan after closure.

closure_assessment.explanation: The episode reached bounded closure: the patient was home on formal discharge medications and prescribed oxygen, the caregiver had separated old medications, knew the follow-up sequence for renal function/electrolytes and cardiology, and knew which symptoms bypass routine follow-up. Residual uncertainty about exact lab values and final disease severity was appropriately left to cardiology follow-up.
